analysis.title: GS FINS & REITs Daily October 2, 2026
key_insights: Futures are higher pre-open (SPX +45bps, NDX +75bps, RTY +60bps) as USTs hold the prior day's gains (2yr unch at 4.79%, 10yr -1bp at 5.23%, 30yr -1bp at 5.60%) and WTI falls 3.75% to $89.40 on reports European countries are discussing releasing diesel stockpiles (France suggested 100mb of diesel plus crude).

Eurozone headline CPI was slightly hotter with core in line, and Tokyo CPI printed very hot across the board. Attention shifts to September NFP at 8:30am, Fed's Logan (10am, voter) and Goolsbee (12pm, non-voter).

S&P Financial Index closed +0.16%, 0.3% below its 200DMA with a 14-day RSI of 27. 66% of S&P Financial stocks finished higher. P&C Insurance, Alts and Insurance Brokers outperformed while Moneycenters, Boutiques and Trust Banks lagged.

Credit bureaus: FHFA is planning to direct Fannie and Freddie to pull credit data from two bureaus instead of three within weeks (Bloomberg, citing a person familiar). Moving from tri-merge to bi-merge cuts volume-related revenue at TRU, EFX and Experian and at FICO. The group traded lower pre-market.

Alts 3Q26 preview: the group is seen as having overshot to the downside against higher rates. The desk sees growth in PE fundraising, AI capex as an underappreciated earnings lever, moderating redemptions in retail private credit funds, and secondary opportunities from DPI issues. Top picks are TPG and STEP on above-average FRE growth, potential upside to consensus and discounted valuations.

Traditional asset managers 3Q26 preview: organic growth rates continue to improve, equity markets are favorable and expense efforts lift margins. Most trade near 10x NTM P/E. Top picks are BLK (organic growth, margin expansion) and BEN (improving flows, alts growth, margin improvement).

Brokers and wealth managers 3Q26 preview: the September hike and forward curve are a tailwind to NII and cash sweep revenue, partly offset by weaker cash balance growth. Organic growth is below trend and competition for advisors is high. The desk sees EPS a mid-single-digit percent below consensus in 3Q. Best risk/reward: LPLA and RJF.

Exchanges 3Q26 preview: strong 3Q volumes imply EPS upside, but stock follow-through is likely limited because of fear of market structure changes from on-chain trading and new products (perps, event contracts, tokenized equities). The analysts see those risks as limited. They favor TW and ICE.

Trust banks 3Q26 preview: NII tailwinds, supportive fees from higher equity markets and volumes, and operating leverage from expenses. AOCI marks under higher rates are a potential headwind. They favor BNY and STT.

CBOE upgraded to Neutral at GS, PT $300. Competition risk, durability of 0DTE SPX volumes and the S&P Global SPX contract extension are seen as diminished risks, near-term volumes are supportive and cash on the balance sheet adds flexibility.

CTRE agreed with LNT Care Development to acquire 45 care homes, a path to a senior housing operating portfolio in the UK. It closed about $488M of other investments since Q2 earnings and raised normalized FFO by 3c at the midpoint to $2.075.
FRT announced the $508M acquisition of The Summit in Alabama, funded with asset sale proceeds, free cash flow and proceeds from recently issued convertible notes.

Payrolls preview: GIR estimates September NFP +80k versus consensus +88k and a three-month average of +71k, private +75k. A late Labor Day and non-repeating August strength in local education and leisure and hospitality (104k combined) argue for a weaker print. Unemployment is seen at 4.0% from 4.1% and average hourly earnings +0.2% m/m, below consensus.

Credit outlook: USD tone weakened on rates volatility and supply focus, with spreads near quarter-end forecasts (USD IG 80bp, USD HY 311bp). GIR sees year-end risk tilted to more widening through early December, though a sharp growth downturn is likely needed for sustained widening. The 2026 USD HY gross issuance forecast was cut to $340bn from $400bn, with $375bn introduced for 2027.

Cross-asset oil tail scenarios: GIR says oil screens well for both tail scenarios because oil implied vols have not returned to prior highs, while rates are a poor expression. In an oil relief scenario equities (S&P 500, Nasdaq, European equities) and FX screen well. In an adverse scenario VIX upside and European equity downside screen best. Their baseline is more benign than market pricing, so they favor higher equities in protected format.
